<!-- pr-reviewer: 271b34b798dfe4f1351bdf2f124c3981a8096b40 -->
**Ready for the maintainer to merge**

Thanks @mkinney - clean, well-argued change.

**What looks good**
- When the default seam is turned, it is kept, so existing wraps stay byte-identical and no golden changes. A turned sheet is re-judged before any cutting (Prime Directive: no unsafe wrap reaches the planner). The 20M straddler cap refuses by name instead of hanging.
- No `unwrap/expect/panic` outside tests in the new files (only a test `expect` at rotary_seam_angle.rs:202); `windows(2)` indexing is guarded; provenance lines present on both new modules.
- `rotary_offset.rs` shrinks (401 to 317 lines); new files are 214 and 154 lines. Motion-only change, no layering, schema, build.rs, .github or dependency changes. Decision file present, body has `Changelog:` and `Fixes #226`, and CHANGELOG.md is untouched.

**Local results (trial-merged with current main, Windows, own target dir)**
| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `camcraft-motion --test rotary_dflat` | 8 passed |
| `--test rotary` | 10 passed |
| `--test rotary_offset` | 9 passed |
| `--test rotary_links` | 7 passed |
| `camcraft-motion --lib` | 155 passed |
| `clippy -p camcraft-motion --all-targets -D warnings` | clean |

Merge with main was automatic, no conflicts.

**Requested before merge**
None.

**Notes (not blocking)**
- Not run here: the Adaptive heavy lane (`rotary_adaptive --ignored`); the author reports its one failure is identical on upstream main.
- This is a `feat`, so it merges at the next minor cut.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
